title: Hypopigmentation & skin of colour
summary: PIH and physiological pigment in skin of colour, plus piebaldism vs vitiligo and the harms of unlicensed bleaching creams.

glance.think: Dark marks after acne/eczema/friction, or milky-white patches — decide hyperpigmentation vs true depigmentation (vitiligo/piebaldism).
glance.engine: Inflammation drives melanin excess (PIH) or autoimmune/congenital melanocyte loss (vitiligo/piebaldism).
glance.backbone: Treat the cause, stop friction and illegal bleaching, daily tinted SPF, azelaic acid/retinoid for PIH; refer vitiligo/piebaldism pathways.
glance.never_miss: Unlicensed steroid/mercury/hydroquinone “fairness” creams — stop and counsel on harm; Waardenburg features with white forelock need hearing assessment.

what: In skin of colour, **post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH)** and constitutional/flexural darkening are everyday presentations. True **depigmentation** (vitiligo, piebaldism) needs a different pathway. This page also flags harm from **unlicensed bleaching and steroid creams**.

list: PIH: any inflammation (acne, eczema, bites, procedures, friction from shaving) leaves excess epidermal ± dermal melanin.
Constitutional pigment: periorbital dark circles, maturational and flexural darkening.
Piebaldism: congenital KIT-pathway melanocyte absence (stable white forelock + patches).
Vitiligo: acquired autoimmune melanocyte loss; associated thyroid and other autoimmunity.

head: Pattern
Clues
rows: Prior inflammation/injury; brown to grey; fades slowly
Children; ill-defined slightly scaly pale patches; hypo- not de-pigmented
Present at birth; white forelock; stable islands of normal skin inside patches
Acquired milky-white patches; Wood’s lamp enhances; may spread

list: History of inflammation, procedures, shaving, cosmetics and bleaching products.
Wood’s lamp: chalk-white sharp edges favour vitiligo/piebaldism over pityriasis alba.
Vitiligo: consider TSH ± antibodies if indicated; piebaldism: genetics/hearing if Waardenburg features.
Cross-check fungal differentials (pityriasis versicolor) when scale is present.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Stable segmental pale patch from early life
Small white shin/arm macules in older adults

list: Treat the driver (acne, eczema, bites). Stop harsh scrubs, lemon juice and bleaching creams.
Hair removal in darker skin: prefer clippers/trimming or accredited long-pulsed Nd:YAG; avoid aggressive IPL settings.
Daily tinted broad-spectrum sunscreen; azelaic acid; topical retinoid off-label; time-limited specialist HQ only.
Vitamin D advice for people with darker skin who avoid sun (UK public-health framing).
Piebaldism: reassurance that it is stable; cosmetic options; genetics if needed — no “repigmenting cream” expectation.
Vitiligo: potent topical steroid or calcineurin inhibitor on limited areas; phototherapy/JAK inhibitors are specialist; camouflage and psychological support.
Refer early for extensive, facial, or rapidly progressive vitiligo.

management.title: Illegal bleaching / steroid creams
management.text: Advise stopping immediately. Counsel on skin atrophy, infection, adrenal suppression and ochronosis. Signpost licensed pathways and Trading Standards/MHRA concerns for supply.

red_flags: Rapidly progressive vitiligo on the face — early dermatology.
White forelock plus deafness/heterochromia → Waardenburg work-up.
Systemic steroid side-effects from bleaching creams — medical review.
pearls: Set timelines: epidermal PIH months; dermal longer.
Ask what people already put on their skin — many worsen PIH with home acids and bleaching.
